description:
## Historical delivery

Commit `7b277ce06b4030e962dda95327e32b72e066f63f` made the then-current source diagnostic checker reuse the shared Types-backed dispatch reachability calculator and added correlated contract-domain rows, bounded-variable closure, guarded coverage, and termination regressions. Those calculator laws remain valuable.

## Superseded policy

The policy that a demanded contracted function must be checked against every declared contract input row, including unobserved alternatives, is no longer authoritative. It violates the demand-driven compiler model by inventing coverage inputs that no demanded activation supplied.

fz-kdt.36.1 owns the final cutover:

- `ActivationInputs` is the sole correlated function-head coverage evidence.
- An applied contract may refine or reject an actual reached row; it is never enumerated as an independent coverage domain.
- Cold functions and unobserved contract alternatives do no coverage work.
- `contract_has_reachable_fail`, `FunctionContract::input_domain_rows` when otherwise unused, and the contract-only `EntryDispatch` wait are removal targets.

The historical prototypes and audit comments below document why correlation, finite closure, and the shared typed reachability calculator were necessary. They do not reinstate whole-contract coverage.

comments.text: AUDIT FAIL on 7212a7820. Blocking: (1) domain coverage Cartesian-products parameter and nested tuple alternatives; a 16-field bool tuple generates 65,536 rows and takes 6.24s, so replace with symbolic/non-expanding analysis; (2) FunctionContract independently unions argument columns and invents cross-overload inputs, so preserve arrow correlation; (3) list projection discards element domains, causing exact @spec count_a([:a]) with []/[:a|tail] to warn; (4) guarded functions still skip analysis entirely, allowing declared inputs to fall through silently. Existing gates/00181 passed, but local correctness is insufficient. No fold; return to implementation and re-audit.

RE-AUDIT FAIL on cumulative 155617973. Remaining blocker: tuple-union correlation is lost across sequential field projection. project_domain unions each field independently; branch_state narrows only the child subject, not its parent union, so later fields reproject the original union and invent {:a,:y}/{:b,:x}. Exact total @spec classify({:a,:x}|{:b,:y}) with two exact clauses still warns. Fix must preserve parent/child correlated alternatives through projection and narrowing, with a production regression; then fresh re-audit.

STEP-BACK: three audits disproved the projection-domain approach. Branch commits 7212a7820, 155617973, 2a427e959 are preserved as failed prototypes and must not be folded. The first lossy boundary is ContractArrow Ty -> KnownSubjectDomain; the second is independent per-SubjectId projected state. fz-1ah.8 now blocks this ticket and will build one root-Ty/evidence dispatch reachability calculator shared with semantic analysis. After .8 lands, restart .1 from integration HEAD and implement diagnostics as a thin consumer; do not salvage boundary heuristics.
